title: Canonical selector for Foundry technology #25 (Capability Router)
problem: Two routers now exist in the kernel line. routing/decision_router.py on claude/opus-maximus-audit-eay0ek returns a RoutingDecision and never invokes a provider. capabilities/router.py on draft PR #70 has select() (decision-only) plus resolve(), which returns chosen.provider() and therefore instantiates code. Final Build Order section 3 forbids multiple active authorities; section 9 and section 12 forbid deleting either. No canonical selector is named, so technology #25 cannot be called closed.
baseline: Before this branch, capabilities/router.py existed only on unmerged draft PR #70; main had no router at all and Foundry technology #25 stood at 'target' in foundry/arsenal.py.

alternatives.name: A: decision router canonical, PR #70 registered as second implementation
alternatives.description: routing/decision_router.py becomes the canonical selector. capabilities/router.py is preserved and registered under FBO section 9 with a written migration path: resolve() moves to a caller holding a capability grant, select() becomes a decision-only adapter, and PR #70's lifecycle machinery (Implementation.origin, LIFECYCLES, restore, set_lifecycle) is rehomed rather than discarded.
advantages: The canonical selector cannot instantiate code, asserted by AST test
PR #70's lifecycle machinery is explicitly retained rather than lost
disadvantages: PR #70 must change before merge, which is another session's branch
Two routers coexist until the founder decides
alternatives.revival_evidence: Adopted as the recorded position on this branch; it is not a founder decision.

alternatives.name: B: PR #70's router canonical, delegating to the decision layer
alternatives.description: capabilities/router.py stays canonical but drops direct provider invocation and delegates selection to routing/decision_router.py before merge.
advantages: Keeps the richer lifecycle model in the canonical position
disadvantages: Requires editing an active branch owned by another session
resolve() has callers whose contract would change
alternatives.revival_evidence: Founder prefers the lifecycle model to hold the canonical position.

alternatives.name: C: merge both into one router
alternatives.description: Combine decision-only selection and lifecycle management into a single new module.
disadvantages: Destroys two working implementations, which FBO section 12 forbids
Highest migration cost and largest review surface
Loses the disagreement that FBO section 4.13 says to preserve
alternatives.revival_evidence: Both routers are proven equivalent on a shared behavioural parity suite and neither dominates in any context.

alternatives.name: D: reversible experiment - run both as registered competitors
alternatives.description: Register both behind one interface and route real work to each, comparing decisions against outcomes as FBO section 4.14 requires.
advantages: Turns the disagreement into evidence rather than argument
Directly satisfies section 9's governed implementation pluralism
disadvantages: There is no real traffic and zero verified outcomes, so the comparison cannot run today
Leaves two active selectors in the meantime, the section 3 condition
alternatives.revival_evidence: The first verified external outcome exists, giving the comparison something to measure.

do_nothing_option.expected_outcome: Two routers remain with no named canonical one. Technology #25 stays open and any claim of router closure stays false.
disadvantages: Leaves exactly the multiple-active-authority condition FBO section 3 forbids
A future session may pick one by accident rather than by decision
Blocks any honest claim that the nervous system is complete

roles.position: The founder's correction was explicit: name one canonical selector and ensure it never invokes providers. Recording the conflict satisfies the second half; only the founder can satisfy the first.
material_concerns: Naming a canonical selector unilaterally would be the agent deciding its own architecture
Leaving it unnamed indefinitely is also a failure of the instruction

roles.position: Decision-only selection and lifecycle management are separable concerns and should not have been fused in one class. Option A separates them correctly; the lifecycle machinery belongs in a registry, not a selector.
material_concerns: Neither router has a typed contract at its boundary

roles.position: Option A's guarantee is narrower than it sounds. The AST test forbids a fixed list of call names (provider, execute, invoke, run, call, apply). A caller can still take the selected candidate_id and invoke it themselves, which the router cannot prevent. The invariant is 'this module does not execute', not 'nothing executes as a result of this module'.
material_concerns: The AST guard is a denylist and can be evaded by a new verb
Decision-only is a property of the module, not of the system
Renaming my class to DecisionRouter removed a collision but not the ambiguity for a reader who sees both

roles.position: Two routers with similar names across two open branches is a live maintenance hazard. The class and test-file collision already occurred and was only caught by reading PR #70's tree.
material_concerns: A merge of both branches would previously have collided on tests/unit/test_capability_router.py
Whoever merges second inherits an unnamed choice
evidence_refs: Both branches originally defined CapabilityRouter and tests/unit/test_capability_router.py

roles.position: No participants and no external effects are involved. The evidence tier here is unit test and static analysis only; neither router has ever routed real work, so no claim about routing quality is supportable in either direction.
material_concerns: Selection weights in both routers are declared, not learned
outcomes_compared() returns 0 and will until a verified outcome exists

evidence.finding: def resolve(self, capability): chosen, _ = self.select(capability); return chosen.provider()

evidence.claim: routing/decision_router.py contains no invocation call site
evidence.finding: AST walk finds no Call to .provider/.execute/.invoke/.run/.call/.apply; DecisionRouter exposes no resolve attribute

evidence.claim: Neither router imports the Consequence Gate
evidence.finding: No policy.consequence_gate or policy.engine import; CI job 3 'One source of authority' passed on 84fab8f9

counterevidence.claim: PR #70's router is simply wrong and should be superseded
counterevidence.finding: It carries machinery the decision router lacks entirely: Implementation.origin with a scorer-blind guarantee, all thirteen FBO section 4.3 lifecycle statuses, set_lifecycle and restore. On preservation grounds it is the richer implementation; only resolve() violates the invariant.

pass_1.intended_outcome: Exactly one named canonical selector for technology #25 that cannot instantiate code, with the other implementation preserved and its migration path written down.

advantages.statement: A decision-only selector cannot become an execution path by accident.
advantages.amplified_value: Makes the section 3 authority boundary structural rather than procedural: there is no code path from selection to execution to review.

advantages.statement: Both implementations are preserved with a written migration path.
advantages.amplified_value: Converts a duplication into governed pluralism per section 9, and keeps PR #70's lifecycle model available for rehoming rather than rediscovery.

disadvantages.statement: The AST guard is a denylist of call names and can be evaded by a verb it does not list.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Bounded and made observable rather than removed: the guard also asserts DecisionRouter has no resolve attribute, so evasion requires adding a new public execution surface, which is visible in the diff. Converted into a review obligation, not a solved problem.

disadvantages.statement: Two routers coexist with no canonical one until the founder decides.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Escalated as BLK-1 in the frozen handoff contract under CONTESTED_UNRESOLVED, recorded in blueprint technology #25's gaps, and asserted by a test that fails if the conflict text is removed. Technology #25 is explicitly not closed.

disadvantages.statement: Decision-only is a property of the module, not of the system: a caller can still invoke the selected candidate.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Accepted and stated. RoutingDecision.explain() ends with the sentence that execution still requires a capability grant and the Consequence Gate, so the boundary is documented at the point of use rather than only in a docstring.

comparisons.baseline: No router on main; technology #25 at 'target' with no implementation. Any router is an improvement on nothing, which is a low bar and not an argument for this one.
comparisons.do_nothing: Two unnamed routers persist. Rejected: it leaves the exact condition section 3 forbids.
comparisons.simplest_viable_alternative: Write no router and let the Composer choose inline. Rejected: it hides selection inside callers, where it cannot be recorded or compared against outcomes as section 4.14 requires.
comparisons.strongest_competing_architecture: Option B, PR #70's router canonical with resolve() removed and selection delegated. Genuinely strong because it keeps the lifecycle model canonical; not chosen here only because editing another session's active branch is not mine to do.
comparisons.reversible_experiment: Option D, register both as competitors and compare decisions against outcomes. Cannot run: zero real traffic, zero verified outcomes.

rejected_alternatives.name: C: merge both into one router
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: Destroys two working implementations and the disagreement between them, which FBO sections 12 and 4.13 forbid.
rejected_alternatives.revival_evidence: A behavioural parity suite shows the two are equivalent in every context tested.

rejected_alternatives.name: D: run both as registered competitors now
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: There is no traffic and no verified outcome, so the comparison has nothing to measure.
rejected_alternatives.revival_evidence: The first verified external outcome exists.

pass_2.attack_summary: Re-attacked Option A as though it were already the canonical answer. The strongest new finding is that 'decision-only' is being used to mean two different things - a module that contains no invocation, and a system in which selection cannot cause execution. Only the first is proven. The second is a property of every caller and is not enforced anywhere.

new_weaknesses.statement: The AST guard enumerates six call names. A future implementation could add a method named dispatch or materialize and pass.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Recorded as a review obligation with a named owner rather than claimed as solved. The complementary assertion (no resolve attribute on the class) means evasion requires a visible new public surface. Not closed.

new_weaknesses.statement: Two similarly named routers across two branches will confuse any reader who encounters them out of order, and the rename to DecisionRouter helps only readers who see both.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: The conflict is written into three places that a reader is likely to hit: the technology #25 binding gaps, the frozen contract's CONTESTED_UNRESOLVED entry, and the PR body. A test fails if the binding text is removed.

new_weaknesses.statement: If the founder chooses Option B, the work on routing/decision_router.py becomes a second implementation to migrate rather than the canonical one.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Accepted as cheap: routing/ is read-only, authority-free and imported by nothing outside its own tests and closure registration. Reverting it is a directory deletion plus one registry line.

new_weaknesses.statement: Naming one canonical selector concentrates a decision that currently has no evidence behind it - neither router has routed anything.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: This is precisely why the verdict is NEEDS_FOUNDER_DECISION rather than RETAIN. Choosing on architectural grounds is legitimate; claiming evidential grounds would not be.

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: A denylist guard cannot be made complete. It is paired with a structural assertion and a review obligation.
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: Any new public method is added to DecisionRouter.

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: Only the founder can name the canonical selector; recording the conflict is the whole of what this branch may do.
System-level non-execution is enforced by the Consequence Gate, not by the router, and that is the correct place for it.
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: A caller is written that acts on a RoutingDecision.

pass_2.final_design: routing/decision_router.py stands as the recorded canonical candidate on this branch: decision-only, AST-asserted, no resolve surface, registered for five-closure verification. capabilities/router.py is preserved untouched with its migration path written into the technology #25 binding. Technology #25 is marked NOT closed in the blueprint, the frozen contract and the pull request. No promotion occurs without a founder decision.

residual_risks.risk: A future session adds an execution verb the AST denylist does not cover.
residual_risks.mitigation: Guard also asserts the absence of a resolve attribute; any new public execution surface appears in the diff.
residual_risks.review_trigger: Any new public method on DecisionRouter.

residual_risks.risk: The conflict record is deleted or softened in a later edit, and #25 silently reads as closed.
residual_risks.mitigation: tests/unit/test_decision_router.py::test_the_router_conflict_is_recorded_rather_than_quietly_settled fails if the gap text loses its markers.

residual_risks.risk: Both branches merge without a decision and two active selectors ship.
residual_risks.mitigation: BLK-1 is in the frozen handoff contract and named in the merge order; ChatGPT's acceptance forbids claiming #25 closed.
residual_risks.review_trigger: Either branch is marked ready for review.

dissent.handling: Recorded and carried forward. The decision does not proceed past recording; no promotion occurs.

entries.position: Calling routing/decision_router.py 'the canonical decision-only selector' overstates what is proven. What is proven is that this module contains no invocation.
entries.rationale: The AST guard is a denylist over six verbs and cannot prove a system-level property.
entries.evidence_threshold: A caller exists that acts on a RoutingDecision without holding a capability grant.
entries.review_trigger: The first caller of DecisionRouter.route outside tests.

entries.position: PR #70's router is the richer implementation and its lifecycle machinery is the part the institution actually lacks; resolve() is the only defect.
entries.rationale: Choosing the thinner module as canonical risks losing the lifecycle model to attrition.
entries.evidence_threshold: The lifecycle machinery is not rehomed within one cycle of a canonical decision.

migration_plan: No migration executes until the founder decides. If Option A is chosen: PR #70 moves resolve() to a caller holding a capability grant, leaves select() as a decision-only adapter over routing/decision_router.py, and rehomes Implementation.origin, LIFECYCLES, set_lifecycle and restore into the Capability Genome Registry (technology #12), which the blueprint already records as lacking all thirteen lifecycle states. If Option B is chosen: routing/decision_router.py is reclassified as a registered second implementation under FBO section 9 and its closure registration is retargeted.

steps: Remove the decision_router registration from closure/nervous_system_registry.py.
Remove the technology #25 evidence references in blueprint/registry.py, leaving the gap text.

kill_criteria: The founder names PR #70's capabilities/router.py canonical and its resolve() is removed.
Every real caller is shown to require instantiation in the same breath as selection, making a decision-only selector unusable.
Two consecutive cycles pass with no caller of DecisionRouter.route outside tests.
review_trigger: Founder names the canonical selector, or either branch is marked ready for review.
